MinebeaMitsumi.why: MinebeaMitsumi makes fan motors for AI servers (including large fan motors for high-heat servers and fans for AI server power supplies) and the miniature ball bearings inside AI-server cooling fans, plus BBU battery protection modules and server fan-motor driver ICs. The company says demand for air cooling from AI data centers remains strong, plans AI-server net sales growth at a CAGR of approx. 22% (FY3/26 - FY3/29), and reports Precision Technologies and air-cooling fans running significantly above initial targets, so its stock benefits directly as AI-server air cooling is built and sold.
MinebeaMitsumi.evidence: Results briefing deck 08-05-2026, 'Five Growth Areas: AI Servers': 'Demand for air cooling remains strong ... Bearings: Secured strong forecasts from major fan motor manufacturers ... Fan motors: Fans for AI server power supplies are performing strongly ... Large fan motors: Rapid increase in new inquiries for high-heat-generating servers'; Q&A (President Yoshida): 'Demand related to air-cooling fans remains strong. Orders for ball bearings and fan motors are extremely solid'.

players.product: fan motors for AI-server air cooling and server power supplies, and miniature ball bearings for AI-server cooling fan motors

quarterly_data.quarter: MinebeaMitsumi results briefing: Financial Results Briefing First Quarter of Fiscal Year Ending March 31, 2027 (08-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: First quarter of the fiscal year ending March 2027 (April-June 2026; results briefing deck): net sales JPY 426.6 billion (+16.3% YoY, +JPY 59.6 billion; -1.3% QoQ) and operating income JPY 26.3 billion (+50.9% YoY; margin 6.2%), both record highs for a first quarter - operating income beat the previous Q1 record (JPY 19.6 billion in FY3/22) by JPY 6.7 billion while absorbing approximately JPY 2.2 billion of special factors (structural reform expenses) in Access Solutions. Profit before taxes JPY 29.8 billion (+91.2%), profit attributable to owners of the parent JPY 21.3 billion (+95.6%), basic EPS JPY 53.03; inventories JPY 432.9 billion at end-June (JPY 391.3 billion at end-March). The company cites strong demand for data center products in Precision Technologies (PT) and Motor, Lighting & Sensing (MLS), while Access Solutions (AS) was hit by the automotive market slowdown; automotive content growth in bearings and motors stayed solid. Average Q1 rate US$1 = JPY 158.80.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 net sales JPY 426.6 billion (+16.3%); operating income JPY 26.3 billion (+50.9%)

quarterly_data.quarter: MinebeaMitsumi results briefing: Financial Results Briefing First Quarter of Fiscal Year Ending March 31, 2027 (08-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Full-year forecast for the fiscal year ending March 2027 (FY3/27; deck): net sales JPY 1,690.0 billion (+1.5%) and operating income JPY 120.0 billion (+15.4%; includes approximately JPY 2.6 billion of restructuring costs) kept unchanged 'from a conservative perspective' (first half JPY 846.5 billion / JPY 53.0 billion, second half JPY 843.5 billion / JPY 67.0 billion); profit before taxes JPY 118.0 billion; profit attributable to owners of the parent revised upward to JPY 87.0 billion (EPS JPY 216.64; +17.8% against FY3/26 excluding special factors). Segment forecasts (net sales / operating income): Precision Technologies JPY 313.0 billion (+11.3%) / JPY 70.0 billion (+12.5%); Motor, Lighting & Sensing JPY 492.0 billion (+7.8%) / JPY 31.0 billion (+15.1%); Semiconductor & Electronics JPY 530.0 billion (-10.2%) / JPY 28.0 billion (+5.0%); Access Solutions JPY 350.0 billion (+5.3%) / JPY 18.5 billion (+8.3%). Sub-segment sales forecasts: ball bearings JPY 198.5 billion, aerospace JPY 32.0 billion, PMC JPY 82.5 billion; motors JPY 376.0 billion, electronic devices JPY 77.0 billion, sensing devices JPY 39.0 billion. Capex forecast JPY 95.0 billion and depreciation and amortisation JPY 75.0 billion (FY3/26: JPY 96.5 billion and JPY 70.4 billion); assumed rate US$1 = JPY 155.00 for Q2-Q4. CEO Kainuma: the strong Q1 did not lead to a raise because the company was criticised in the past for raising forecasts early in the term and then missing; given the uncertain macro environment it kept the initial guidance out of an extremely conservative approach.
quarterly_data.figure: FY3/27 forecast: net sales JPY 1,690.0 billion; operating income JPY 120.0 billion (unchanged); profit attributable JPY 87.0 billion (raised)

quarterly_data.quarter: MinebeaMitsumi results briefing: Financial Results Briefing First Quarter of Fiscal Year Ending March 31, 2027 (08-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Ball bearings (deck + CEO in the Q&A): Q1 average external sales volume of 310 million units/month and production of 340 million units/month were both record highs; data center demand stayed strong and exceeded expectations, and the company expects the record momentum to continue in the second half; keeping and expanding market share is the priority. Capacity plan (million units/month): 404 in FY3/26, 424 in FY3/27, 444 in FY3/28 and 476 in FY3/29 - approximately JPY 9 billion for repurposing and relocating existing equipment at the Thailand plant and upgrading equipment at the plants in Thailand and Singapore, and approximately JPY 50 billion for the start-up of a new plant and its manufacturing equipment. CEO Kainuma: production capacity is tight at MinebeaMitsumi and at its competitors, causing a market-wide supply shortage, and customers expanding their business are asking for more volume; the company has not announced a flat across-the-board price hike but has started field-level price negotiations for urgent additional demand (centred on the applications and customers with the most robust demand) while keeping its long-term priority customers, and expects average selling prices to rise gradually as a 'law of nature'. He adds that B2B customers increasingly value delivery speed, performance and supply reliability rather than price alone.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 bearing external sales 310 million units/month, production 340 million units/month; capacity 476 million units/month planned for FY3/29

quarterly_data.quarter: MinebeaMitsumi results briefing: Financial Results Briefing First Quarter of Fiscal Year Ending March 31, 2027 (08-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: AI servers, one of the company's 'Five Growth Areas' (deck): demand for air cooling remains strong and liquid-cooling demand is to become a future growth driver. Bearings secured strong forecasts from major fan motor manufacturers; HDD spindle motor demand is solid, centred on nearline HDDs; fans for AI server power supplies are performing strongly; large fan motors see a rapid increase in new inquiries for high-heat-generating servers; battery protection modules for BBUs rise substantially this fiscal year on surging AI-server power-supply demand; inquiries for liquid-cooling electric pumps and valves are gaining full momentum. Its AI-server products: pressure sensors (strain gage), large fan motors, BBU battery protection modules, airflow sensors, fan motors, water leak sensors, pump motors, stepping motors (valve opening/closing), EEPROM and HDD pivots and spindle motors. Planned AI-server net sales CAGR approx. 22% (FY3/26 - FY3/29). President Yoshida: orders for ball bearings and fan motors are extremely solid, PT and air-cooling fans in particular are running significantly above initial targets and bearing profitability has improved substantially; liquid-cooling negotiations for coolant control valves, pump motors and water leak sensors are advancing in line with customer development schedules, but liquid cooling is not heavily factored into the full-year forecast because its adoption lags air cooling.
quarterly_data.figure: AI-server net sales CAGR approx. 22% (FY3/26 - FY3/29)

quarterly_data.quarter: MinebeaMitsumi results briefing: Financial Results Briefing First Quarter of Fiscal Year Ending March 31, 2027 (08-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Motor, Lighting & Sensing (deck): spindle and fan motors stay strong on robust AI server demand and motor profitability improved; demand for fans in solar power applications keeps growing, led by Europe, amid rising energy costs; automotive seat fans and related products are expanding with luxury-seat demand (the company also proposes BLDC motors for seat slide and recline and resonant devices for warning vibrations). Electronic devices: demand for BBU battery protection modules stays strong with the AI server market, and to boost capacity new production is scheduled to launch at the Mexico plant this October. Sensing devices: inquiries for 'MINEGE' thin-film copper strain gages and joint torque sensors for humanoid robots are rising.
quarterly_data.figure: BBU battery protection module production at the Mexico plant scheduled from October

quarterly_data.quarter: MinebeaMitsumi results briefing: Financial Results Briefing First Quarter of Fiscal Year Ending March 31, 2027 (08-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Semiconductors (deck + Q&A): lithium-ion battery protection ICs, mainly for mid- to high-end smartphones, stay strong; EEPROMs for AI servers (for DRAM/DIMM and SSDs) and medical ICs perform well; adoption of the company's driver ICs for server fan motors is gaining momentum; power semiconductors (IGBTs/diodes) and analog ICs for AI servers (reset ICs, LDO/DC-DC ICs, eFuse ICs, temperature sensor ICs, airflow sensors) are under development and expansion. The Shiga Plant produces lithium-ion protection ICs, MEMS and IGBTs (including foundry production) and aims for monthly profitability within this fiscal year; in-house IGBT output is set to increase. President Yoshida: analog semiconductors are steady while power semiconductors struggle, mainly on capacity-utilisation losses at the Shiga Plant; he expects the semiconductor business to recover from next fiscal year, on track for the medium-term forecast. CEO Kainuma: he instructed teams to ask customers for price revisions, particularly for analog semiconductors where the company has competitive advantages; the largest driver of the power-semiconductor weakness was the complete cancellation of an EV power semiconductor program for a specific customer; the company will accelerate development of 'Fin-SiC', its next-generation SiC power semiconductor, and widen sales of power semiconductors for power-supply peripherals across industrial and consumer applications beyond EVs.

quarterly_data.quarter: MinebeaMitsumi results briefing: Financial Results Briefing First Quarter of Fiscal Year Ending March 31, 2027 (08-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Optical devices and mechanical components (SE; deck + Q&A): optical device profitability kept recovering, with a real operating margin of 7% in Q1, and mechanical components started better than expected in both sales and profit. CEO Kainuma: the optical-device ramp is smoother than expected because line switching from older to newer models is running ahead of plan, not because of a market-share shift against the competitor; two years ago launch problems caused a temporary share loss, which did not recur this year. President Yoshida: profitability measures are showing results in both businesses, but next term's plans will keep conservative assumptions.
quarterly_data.figure: optical devices real operating margin 7% in Q1

quarterly_data.quarter: MinebeaMitsumi results briefing: Financial Results Briefing First Quarter of Fiscal Year Ending March 31, 2027 (08-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Precision Technologies, aerospace and PMC (deck + Q&A): aerospace sales stayed solid on strong aircraft demand, and price revisions on renewal of long-term agreements (LTAs) drove a record-high operating margin in Q1, with further improvement expected from the second half; 'Aerospace' replaces 'Aircraft' as the '+1' growth area to expand in the space industry (hybrid ceramic ball bearings for satellite reaction wheel assemblies, double-row angular contact ball bearings for laser communication terminals, roller bearings for rocket fuel-supply pre-valves, bearings for throttle valves and turbo pumps, SOS-type pressure sensors for rocket engines and liquid hydrogen / liquid oxygen tanks). PMC: demand for HDD applications stayed solid and sales of automotive components for LiDAR grew. CEO Kainuma on HDD components: customer contracts pass raw-material increases into selling prices, but base prices have not been raised although major HDD customers are performing strongly.

quarterly_data.quarter: MinebeaMitsumi results briefing: Financial Results Briefing First Quarter of Fiscal Year Ending March 31, 2027 (08-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Access Solutions (deck + Q&A): President Yoshida says Q1 fell short of plan because automotive markets in Europe and China were tougher than expected, not because of restructuring; the segment booked over JPY 2.0 billion of structural reform costs in Q1 while the roughly JPY 0.5 billion gain on site sales planned against JPY 2.2 billion of restructuring slipped to later in the year (the sales are still expected this fiscal year, so the full year stays on plan). Mass production of the BMW 'Winglet' (formerly the wing handle), adopted for the new BMW X5 announced on June 30, began in August; CEO Kainuma expects profit contribution within a month or two and growing volumes and profit toward the second half. The impact of China's flush-handle regulations was minimised through alternative proposals; structural reforms in Europe continue; the two-wheel business stays solid, centred on Southeast Asia; the US and Asia-Pacific remain resilient and the segment's eight business units include industrial machinery.
quarterly_data.figure: over JPY 2.0 billion of structural reform costs in Q1

quarterly_data.quarter: MinebeaMitsumi results briefing: Financial Results Briefing First Quarter of Fiscal Year Ending March 31, 2027 (08-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Humanoid robots, one of the 'Five Growth Areas' (deck): bearings won large orders for body applications, primarily from major US companies; numerous inquiries for small to medium-sized custom small DC motors for hands and bodies; torque/force sensors entered the joint-application market; ball screws drew inquiries for hand applications and a mass-production system is being set up; PMC is cultivating demand for body components. The company's net sales outlook chart (its own estimates using market research reports) shows JPY 10.0 billion in FY3/29 and JPY 100.0 billion (standard case) or JPY 200.0 billion (upside case) in FY3/35, an upside-case CAGR of approx. 65% (FY3/29-FY3/35).
quarterly_data.figure: humanoid-robot net sales upside-case CAGR approx. 65% (FY3/29-FY3/35)
